en: The Hymn to Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa
O Śrīnivāsa, O Lord of the Universe, O Śrī Hari, you who are affectionate toward your devotees!
O Consort of Lakṣmī, salutations to you; protect me from the ocean of worldly existence. 1.
O Rādhāramaṇa, O Govinda, O fulfiller of the desires of devotees, O Nārāyaṇa, salutations to You; protect me from the ocean of worldly existence! 2.
O Dāmodara, O most noble one, O dispeller of all calamities, O Hṛṣīkeśa, salutations to you; protect me from the ocean of worldly existence! 3.
O Garuḍa-bannered one, O dweller of Vaikuṇṭha, O Keśava, O Acyuta, O Janārdana, salutations to you; protect me from the ocean of worldly existence! 4.
O bearer of the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, marked with the Śrīvatsa, dark as a rain cloud, salutations to you; protect me from the ocean of worldly existence. 5.
You are my mother, you are my father, you are my kinsman, you are the true guru, and a treasure-house of compassion;
there is no other supreme deity besides you—save me from the ocean of worldly existence! 6.
I know nothing of the practice of charity, religious duty, and so forth, nor of yoga, sacrifice, austerity, or recitation;
you alone must show compassion and save me from the ocean of worldly existence. (7)
Though there may be no evildoer equal to me, yet there is no remover of sin equal to you.
O witness of all things, I have made this petition; lift up me, your fallen and afflicted one, before your very presence. (8)
Thus ends the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa Stotra composed by Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
